cards.front: Define the nth partial sum $s_n$ of the series $\sum_{k=1}^\infty a_k$.
State the precise definition of convergence for an infinite series $\sum a_k$.
cards.back: The series converges to $L$ if $\lim_{n\to\infty} s_n = L$ where $L$ is finite; otherwise it diverges.

cards.front: Give the closed-form expression for the partial sum $s_n$ of the geometric series $\sum_{k=0}^n r^k$ when $r\ne 1$.
The partial sums of the harmonic series satisfy $s_n > \ln(n+1)$. What does this imply for convergence?
cards.back: Since $\ln(n+1)\to\infty$, $s_n\to\infty$, so the harmonic series diverges.

cards.front: Prove: if $\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n \ne 0$, then $\sum a_k$ diverges.
cards.back: Suppose the series converges. Then $s_n\to L$ finite, so $a_{n+1}=s_{n+1}-s_n	o L-L=0$, contradiction. Hence diverges.

cards.front: If $s_n=1-\frac1n$, find $\sum_{k=1}^\infty a_k$ or state if it diverges.
What occurs if the sequence of partial sums $\{s_n\}$ is bounded but does not converge?
cards.back: The series diverges (e.g., $s_n=(-1)^n$). Boundedness alone is insufficient for convergence.
